stage: round 9 group R9-F1.6 (#1647, #1659): the coordinator findings D1-s2-02, D1-s1-03 and D14-s1-01

carries.from: the pull request that lands round 9's F4.1 (roster group R9-F4.1: part of #1644, fixes #1684 and #1673) -- one state-stamp owner, a plausibility window on temperature inputs, the quiet-store staleness horizon, the flow-lift supply ceiling and the sysid sizing headroom
carries.control: Established by measurement with its null control. The finders' sentinel harness fed DS18B20 fault codes (-127 and 85) through `InputReader.read` on 12 key/value cells; at F4.1's merge base 12 of 12 read as healthy values, at its head 2 of 12 do: 85 on DHW and on the buffer tank, which stay legal because a tank can be at 85 degC. A plausible 21.3 degC reads as healthy on every key in both trees (null control).
carries.remeasure: Do not trust these counts: they are measured at F4.1's head. Read `INPUT_PLAUSIBLE_RANGE_C` in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/const.py and `plausible_c` in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/inputs.py, then re-run tests/features.py and read its `R9 P2` section.
carries.brief: The plausibility window is `const.INPUT_PLAUSIBLE_RANGE_C`, read only through `inputs.plausible_c(key, value_c)`; a reading outside it becomes the input problem `implausible`, which counts in `missing_keys` and freezes the learners. Use that function and do not add a second range table. The window refuses sensor fault codes, not plant states: 85 degC stays legal in the DHW and buffer tanks.

carries.from: the pull request that lands round 9's F4.1 (roster group R9-F4.1: part of #1644, fixes #1684 and #1673) -- one state-stamp owner, a plausibility window on temperature inputs, the quiet-store staleness horizon, the flow-lift supply ceiling and the sysid sizing headroom
carries.control: Established by measurement with its null control. F4.1 moved the indoor, lower-floor, floor-return, buffer and DHW temperatures from a 60 min to a 360 min staleness limit (`QUIET_STORE_MAX_AGE_MINUTES`), because a healthy report-on-change probe went 4 h 15 min between reports in the field. The finder's silence harness (tools/audit/round9/D1/leads/indoor_silence.py) reads `unavailable` on 4 of 7 silence cells at the merge base and on 1 of 7 at the head (480 min). The null control is a probe that re-reports: it reads 0 unavailable in both trees. The cost is the other side of the same number. A probe that dies without going unavailable now holds its last value as fresh for up to 6 h instead of 1 h, and the learners gated by `coordinator._learning_frozen` train on that flatline for as long.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust these counts: they are measured at F4.1's head. Read `QUIET_STORE_MAX_AGE_MINUTES` in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/const.py, then read which input problems `coordinator._learning_frozen` freezes on in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py. Drive one learning interval with an indoor state frozen at one value and last reported 300 min ago, and confirm the learner still folds it.
carries.brief: The quiet-store horizon is a watchdog limit, and the learners borrowed it. Only `coordinator._learning_frozen` can give them a shorter one: freeze learning on a slow-store input whose value has not moved for longer than the learner can tolerate (the old 60 min is the measured baseline), while the reading itself stays available to the plan up to `QUIET_STORE_MAX_AGE_MINUTES`. Keep the two limits separate. Shortening the watchdog again reopens #1684 (N-staleness), which F4.1 closed. The fix review of F4.1 assigned this to F1.
